key_insight: Replace explicit bi-temporal differencing with a parameter-free feature exchange inside a Siamese encoder–decoder pipeline (SEED), enabling direct cross-temporal interaction while keeping the model simple and shared-weighted.
problem_solved: Remote sensing change detection typically relies on bespoke difference modules (subtraction, concatenation) to fuse bi-temporal features, increasing architectural complexity and tuning burden. SEED addresses the need for a simpler, more streamlined fusion mechanism that still discriminates changes effectively.
method: Siamese encoders with shared weights process the two temporal images to produce comparable feature maps.
Parameter-free feature exchange swaps/ merges features across the two temporal streams (instead of computing explicit differences) to enable direct cross-temporal interaction.
A decoder consumes the exchanged features to predict the change map, keeping the overall pipeline lightweight and modular.
impact: SEED simplifies model design for change detection, reducing architectural complexity and hyperparameter tuning while enabling straightforward incorporation into existing pipelines—useful for practitioners seeking efficient, robust bi-temporal fusion.
